title: SLA-Bound Tiered Reservation Flow & Capacity Routing Playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a prescriptive provisioning workflow and decision playbook for dedicated capacity reservations that binds throughput SLAs to reservation tiers, routes requests based on workload characteristics, and defines autoscaling guardrails. The output is a single living document + request form and acceptance criteria that will be used by Sales/CS to submit reservations and by Capacity Ops to approve/provision. This ticket scopes: (1) reservation tiers and their throughput/latency SLOs, (2) approval matrix and automated gating checks, (3) autoscaling policy defaults and max-burst rules per tier, (4) routing rules for mixed workloads (latency-sensitive vs batch), (5) forecasting inputs for capacity planning (demand curves, headroom assumptions), and (6) handoff checklist to infra for provisioning and billing integration.
acceptance_criteria: Define at least three reservation tiers (Bronze, Silver, Gold) with explicit throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) and max P95 latency targets
Design reservation request form fields required for automated eligibility checks (expected QPS, median seq length, peak tort, region, compliance needs)
Approval matrix created: who approves what (Sales < $50k/month, RevOps + Security for > $50k/month or compliance-required), with clear SLA for approval turnaround
Autoscaling policy templates drafted per tier: baseline capacity, scale-up cooldown, scale-down window, max burst factor, cost cap knob
Routing rules documented for preferring low-latency pools for latency-sensitive workloads and high-throughput pools for batch/throughput workloads
Handoff checklist with observable dashboards, billing codes, runbook links, and a verification plan for end-to-end latency and throughput tests
estimate_breakdown: Discovery (2): finalize tiers and gating checks; Form + API (3): request schema + validation; Ops Playbook (2): approval matrix + handoff checklist; QA + Runbook (1): test plan and dashboards
notes: We need to balance commercial simplicity with operational safety. Early decision: use three tiers to keep SKU count low; optional add-ons for burst and dedicated HSM for security-sensitive customers. Cost-estimation model will be parametric: (reserved_gpus * hours * gpu_rate) + expected egress + autoscale_burst_headroom factor.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed to model tiers around expected tokens/sec per GPU, not pure GPU counts. Luca to prototype request schema by end of week.

2025-02-24 - Luca Moreno: Drafted reservation request schema in Confluence. Key open question: whether to require customers to submit a representative prompt set for throughput verification. Ops prefers synthetic load profiles to speed approval.

2025-02-28 - Priya Desai (RevOps): Approval thresholds look reasonable; request adding a required billing code field. Also suggested an expedited review path for existing enterprise customers with past usage > $200k/month.

2025-03-03 - Engineering feedback (ENG-2134): Autoscale cooldown of 60s may be too aggressive for chat workloads; proposal to use 90s for Gold/latency-sensitive tiers. Also noted the need for graceful fallback routes to hosted model variants when capacity constraints hit.

2025-03-05 - Aisha Khan: Updated playbook to include a mandatory pre-provisioning smoke test (10-minute synthetic workload) and an itemized billing preview. Marking this ticket as In Progress and assigning provisioning tasks to Capacity Ops once the form is live.
implementation_steps: Finalize tier definitions and numeric SLOs
Implement reservation request schema and validation rules (API + Console)
Create automated gating checks (quota, compliance flags, billing code)
Publish approval matrix and contact routing for manual approvals
Build autoscale policy templates and attach to provisioned pools
Add dashboards and smoke-test jobs to the handoff checklist
Run a staged pilot with 3 customers to validate end-to-end flow
